The head arm is re-derived independently at the reviewed head aae8ae18 in a scratch tree (logs/review-head-gate.log: 10 passed, EXIT=0, no FAILED or ERROR id), so added failures are a subset of an empty head-failure set and the run provably added none. The one failure in the reviewed negative-control.log and in my reproduced control log (logs/negative-control-repro.log) is the declared keying mutation, not a gate arm.

findings.text: follow-on: the signal withholding path adds `and rule.transformation != "one_like"`, an exemption the plan prose does not state ("skips each binding or rule that targets a COCOS-dependent path while its source COCOS is undeclared"; "An undeclared source COCOS is still a refusal by default"). It is load-bearing: of the 61 JT-60SA signal rules, 32 target a COCOS-dependent path with undeclared source COCOS and every one declares transformation one_like, so the literal rule withholds 32 signals and the exemption withholds none, while the done-when demands exactly the two poloidal_angle bindings. The exemption is physically defensible (a one_like factor is 1.0, never assumed) but the plan text and the code now disagree.

follow-on: the binding branch withholds on any COCOS-dependent target with undeclared COCOS, while the signal branch at :375 exempts one_like; a binding whose target carries a one_like COCOS label and an undeclared source COCOS would be dropped where the equivalent signal is kept. No JT-60SA binding reaches this case (the run withholds only the two pol_angle_like poloidal_angle bindings), so the asymmetry is latent rather than exercised.

follow-on: _validator_command was changed from shutil.which("tokamap-validator") with a "python3" fallback to always sys.executable -c "from tokamap.validator.main import run; run()". This alters an existing test mechanism, not only adding coverage; it is inside the write path and arguably a fix (the dropped import was otherwise unused), but it is beyond the goal's stated change.

follow-on: the commit removes two blank lines and at :581 reflows an existing raise click.ClickException, and imas_ambix/data/tokamap_export.py:236 reflows an existing canonical_factor call; pure formatting of untouched lines rides in a feature commit, adding review noise the goal does not imply.

follow-on: the manifest declares docs/figures/jt60sa-tokamap-from-generated-maps/tokamap-export-command as a write path but no figure was produced, and the evidence fragment carries none, contrary to the mandate that research and evidence documents be illustrated where a graphic aids understanding (the six-group, two-partition, 172-entry structure and the 17-probe resolution are natural candidates).
